reader_notes: Q1 option C ends '…though only a raised wreck can be studied', which sits in mild tension with the passage's own account of in-situ work (Renlund cored the wreck 'without disturbing' it). It is still unambiguously the best main-idea option — A and B are supporting details and D is contradicted — so the item resolves, but the wording overstates.
Mixed units: depth given as 'ninety metres' but the timber's origin as 'hundreds of miles' away. A student reading closely may notice the inconsistency; it does not affect any answer.
